title: Argue with Me Tersely: Towards Sentence-Level Counter-Argument Generation
authors: Jiayu Lin; Rong Ye; Meng Han; Qi Zhang; Ruofei Lai; Xinyu Zhang; Zhao Cao; Xuanjing Huang; Zhongyu Wei
task_description: Generate concise sentence-level counter-arguments to an input argument and evaluate them with human-preference-informed judging.
inputs: Argument/post from the ChangeMyView debate forum; manually annotated counter-argument data.
outputs_or_labels: Sentence-level counter-argument; human preference data and Arg-Judge evaluation.
pipeline_gap_filled: direct counterargument generation; concise response quality
authenticity_class: authentic online debate with manual annotation
artifact_access_status: ACL page states code and data are available; repository URL identified; contents not independently rerun
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states ArgTersely is a benchmark for sentence-level counter-argument generation, based on manually annotated ChangeMyView data, with code/data release and a learned evaluator.
limitations: Sentence-level output is narrower than multi-turn rebuttal; no typed scholastic stages, source-grounded evidence, or objection-to-reply alignment labels.
why_relevant: Strongest direct generation benchmark for concise counter-argument response quality.

title: Retrieval of the Best Counterargument without Prior Topic Knowledge
authors: Henning Wachsmuth; Shahbaz Syed; Benno Stein
task_description: Retrieve the best counterargument for an input argument under same-debate, same-theme, and whole-portal candidate pools.
inputs: Argument plus candidate counterarguments from iDebate.
outputs_or_labels: Binary best-counterargument relevance pairs; train/validation/test splits.
pipeline_gap_filled: counterargument retrieval; hard negatives for generation
artifact_access_status: verified dataset landing page; download linked from Webis/Zenodo
license_status: not stated on retained landing-page evidence
evidence_basis: Paper reports 6,753 argument/best-counterargument pairs and multiple candidate-pool retrieval tasks; official Webis page confirms corpus identity.
limitations: Retrieval rather than free-form generation; portal-curated best labels do not encode response stages or objection types.
why_relevant: Excellent ranking and candidate-selection control before generation.

title: Knowledge-Enhanced Evidence Retrieval for Counterargument Generation
authors: Yohan Jo; Haneul Yoo; JinYeong Bak; Alice Oh; Chris Reed; Eduard Hovy
task_description: Retrieve sentence-level counterevidence to a statement through document retrieval, ranking, sentence selection, and knowledge-enhanced NLI.
inputs: Argumentative statement; web documents and candidate sentences; CauseNet/Wikidata-enhanced inference.
authenticity_class: authentic web evidence plus curated NLI resources
artifact_access_status: official GitHub public; data directory present
license_status: not stated in retained repository evidence
evidence_basis: ACL paper and official repository describe the counterevidence retrieval pipeline and expose code/data.
limitations: Targets evidence to statements rather than full argument-level rebuttals; no regulated dialogue stages or response-quality rubric.
why_relevant: Direct precedent for retrieving evidence that can instantiate an objection or rebuttal.

citation: Kiesel et al. / Touché at CLEF (2025)
title: Touché at CLEF 2025 — Retrieval-Augmented Debating
authors: Martin Potthast; Henning Wachsmuth; Touché organizers
task_description: In a four-turn simulated debate, retrieve counterarguments to the user or supporting evidence for the attacked system response, then generate the next response.
inputs: U1,S1,U2,S2,U3,S3,U4,S4 dialogue state; approximately 300,000 ClaimRev arguments.
outputs_or_labels: Next-utterance responses evaluated for Quantity, Quality, Relation, and Manner; toy datasets and TIRA submissions.
pipeline_gap_filled: stage-conditioned retrieval; counterargument-vs-support routing; response generation
authenticity_class: authentic argument collection with simulated multi-turn protocol
artifact_access_status: official task page and data/API/index links verified
license_status: not stated on retained task-page evidence
evidence_basis: Official task page defines the four-turn sequence, alternating retrieval target, response limit, collection size, and evaluation criteria.
limitations: Response-level shared-task evaluation lacks a typed scholastic objection taxonomy and uses simulated user turns.
why_relevant: Closest found benchmark to role-aware, stage-conditioned argument-response generation.

title: Benchmarking Critical Questions Generation: A Challenging Reasoning Task for Large Language Models
task_description: Generate critical questions that expose assumptions and challenge the validity of argumentative reasoning structures.
inputs: Argumentative text and scheme-conditioned context; about 5,000 manually annotated questions.
outputs_or_labels: Valid/useful critical questions; reference-based and human-aligned evaluation; public leaderboard.
pipeline_gap_filled: structured challenge/objection generation; scheme-conditioned response planning
artifact_access_status: ACL page states data/code and leaderboard; official repository identified
license_status: ACL publication license is known; dataset terms not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states the first large-scale dataset of about 5K manually annotated questions, reference-based evaluation, 11-model baseline, and data/code release.
limitations: Generates questions rather than rebuttal prose or complete replies; answer-to-question closure is not scored.
why_relevant: Best direct benchmark for structured, assumption-targeting objection generation.

title: Overview of the Critical Questions Generation Shared Task
authors: Blanca Calvo Figueras; Jaione Bengoetxea; Maite Heredia; Ekaterina Sviridova; Elena Cabrio; Serena Villata; Rodrigo Agerri
task_description: Shared-task evaluation of LLMs generating critical questions that identify fallacious or inadequately constructed arguments.
outputs_or_labels: Critical-question generation scores; 13 team submissions and shared-task rankings.
artifact_access_status: official ACL paper and shared-task description verified; task package not independently rerun
evidence_basis: ACL overview states 13 teams, maximum accuracy 67.6, and that three of four top systems used scheme annotations.
limitations: Question generation is an upstream challenge, not rebuttal completion or one-to-one reply coverage.
why_relevant: Provides a reproducible shared-task framing and evidence that argument-form labels improve structured challenge generation.

title: Critical Questions Generation: Motivation and Challenges
task_description: Defines critical-question generation from argumentative text using Walton templates and LLM-generated questions.
inputs: Argumentative text instantiated with Walton schemes; template and LLM-generated questions.
outputs_or_labels: Valid critical questions and generation evaluation procedures.
artifact_access_status: ACL paper/PDF verified; artifact package not independently located
evidence_basis: ACL abstract defines the task and two construction methods, and motivates it as a safer alternative to knowledge-heavy counterargument generation.
limitations: Precursor task/resource; no full response generation, evidence retrieval, or rebuttal evaluation.
why_relevant: Clarifies the structured-response target and supplies Walton-style question semantics.

title: ArgGenBench: Benchmarking the Complex Controlled Argument Generation Capability of Large Language Models
task_description: Generate arguments under joint controls for topic, stance, length, style, strategy, audience, and key points.
inputs: Complex multi-dimensional generation instructions and human-verified references.
outputs_or_labels: Controlled arguments; win rate against human-verified references; evaluation across 15 LLMs.
artifact_access_status: ACL paper verified; artifact URL/package not independently confirmed
evidence_basis: ACL abstract identifies the seven control dimensions, 15-model evaluation, and best-model 42.7% win rate against human-verified references.
limitations: Not specifically counterargument/rebuttal or dialogue-stage conditioned; control dimensions omit explicit attack target and reply alignment.
why_relevant: Strong current benchmark for multi-constraint argument generation that can be adapted to response roles.

title: ArgBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Computational Argumentation Tasks
authors: Yamen Ajjour; Carlotta Quensel; Nedim Lipka; Henning Wachsmuth
task_description: Unifies 33 prior datasets into 46 computational-argumentation tasks spanning mining, perspective, quality, reasoning, and generation.
inputs: Task-specific argumentation datasets, instructions, and splits.
outputs_or_labels: Task labels/outputs for 46 tasks; prompting and leave-one-task-out evaluation setups.
pipeline_gap_filled: umbrella controls for structured argument generation and response quality
authenticity_class: mixed inherited authentic and synthetic argument resources
artifact_access_status: official ACL paper and Webis repository public; component access varies
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states 33 datasets, 46 tasks, five skill areas, and standardized evaluation.
limitations: Not dedicated to rebuttal stages; heterogeneous component tasks complicate construct validity and task-specific artifact checking.
why_relevant: Best umbrella inventory for discovering reusable response-generation, quality, and reasoning tasks.

title: LLM DEBATE OPPONENT: Counter-argument Generation focusing on Implicit and Critical Premises
authors: Taisei Ozaki; Chihiro Nakagawa; Naoya Inoue; Shoichi Naito; Kenshi Yamaguchi
task_description: Compare one-step and multi-step counter-argument generation methods, targeting implicit and critical premises across 100 debate topics.
inputs: 100 debate topics, debate motions, explicit/implicit premise targets.
outputs_or_labels: Generated counterarguments with expert and automated evaluations.
artifact_access_status: ACL paper verified; reusable dataset package not independently located
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states systematic comparison across 100 topics and evaluates premise-targeting strategies with expert and automated measures.
limitations: Study/evaluation design rather than a clearly released benchmark; no typed argument graph or rebuttal-stage labels.
why_relevant: Important failure-mode control for whether replies attack implicit as well as explicit premises.

title: Socratic Question Generation: A Novel Dataset, Models, and Evaluation
authors: Beng Heng Ang; Sujatha Das Gollapalli; See-Kiong Ng
task_description: Generate type-sensitive Socratic questions that elicit reasoning and alternate views from context.
inputs: About 110K question-context pairs; 105K labeled train/dev/test pairs.
outputs_or_labels: Question-type labels; BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, BERTScore/BLEURT, and human evaluation.
artifact_access_status: ACL paper/PDF verified; artifact access not independently checked
evidence_basis: ACL abstract/PDF states dataset scale, question types, automatic metrics, and human evaluation.
limitations: Questions are not themselves rebuttals and the corpus does not encode answer determination or reply coverage.
why_relevant: Practical upstream benchmark for relevant, type-appropriate, non-redundant objections.

title: High Quality Real-Time Structured Debate Generation
authors: Authors listed in retained local review
task_description: Generate or evaluate real-time structured debate using tree-structured argument metadata.
inputs: Tree-structured debate corpus with argument metadata.
outputs_or_labels: Structured debate responses and generation-quality judgments.
artifact_access_status: local retained summary identifies the resource; stable artifact URL not independently verified
evidence_basis: Local benchmark_studies.csv and retained summary classify a tree-structured debate corpus used for generation evaluation.
limitations: Exact paper identity/artifact route was not independently re-resolved in this pass; generation evaluation is not explicitly rebuttal-typed.
why_relevant: Relevant precedent for tree-structured rather than flat response generation, but access failure is preserved.

title: ConQRet: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Argumentation with LLM Judges
authors: Kaustubh D. Dhole; Kai Shu; Eugene Agichtein
task_description: Evaluate retrieval-augmented argumentation over controversial questions, including retrieval effectiveness, argument quality, and groundedness.
inputs: 98 controversial topics; about 6,500 scraped web documents; expert-authored ProCon arguments; stance-conditioned queries.
outputs_or_labels: Relevant-document judgments, stance-conditioned evidence, generated arguments, and fine-grained judge dimensions.
pipeline_gap_filled: grounded counterargument support and response quality
artifact_access_status: official paper and repository available; dataset download gated by repository instructions
evidence_basis: Paper abstract and official repository specify topics/documents, stance-conditioned evidence, retrieval, and grounded argument generation.
limitations: No multi-turn objection/rebuttal protocol; stance is not a discourse role or attack-history state.
why_relevant: Strong grounding and quality complement to direct counterargument-generation benchmarks.

title: RPC-Bench: A Fine-grained Benchmark for Research Paper Comprehension
authors: Yelin Chen; Fanjin Zhang; Suping Sun; Yunhe Pang; Yuanchun Wang; Jian Song; XiaoYan Li; Lei Hou; Shu Zhao; Jie Tang; Juanzi Li
task_description: Evaluate fine-grained comprehension and claim verification over authentic peer-review/rebuttal exchanges.
inputs: OpenReview papers plus review-rebuttal exchanges; text and rendered-page inputs.
artifact_access_status: official ACL paper, project page, and GitHub identified; data-download workflow documented
license_status: code Apache-2.0; dataset terms require separate check
evidence_basis: ACL and official project sources describe review-rebuttal provenance, benchmark taxonomy, and released workflow.
limitations: QA comprehension rather than response generation or retrieval ranking; peer-review rebuttal is a specialized domain.
why_relevant: Useful rebuttal-specific obligation and claim-response alignment control.

title: Evaluating large language models’ ability to generate interpretive arguments
task_description: Collect and evaluate human- and model-generated arguments for and against interpretations of ambiguous rules and scenarios.
inputs: Professional-ethics rules, ambiguous scenarios, human arguments, and LLM arguments.
outputs_or_labels: Human ratings of quality/persuasiveness and human-vs-machine discrimination.
pipeline_gap_filled: two-sided argument generation and human response-quality evaluation
authenticity_class: human-authored rules/scenarios plus human and model arguments
artifact_access_status: open-access paper/PDF verified; underlying dataset not independently located
license_status: CC BY-NC 4.0 stated on official page
evidence_basis: Official SAGE abstract describes curated rules/scenarios, arguments for/against interpretations, quality/persuasiveness evaluation, and Turing-style comparison.
limitations: Legal/ethical interpretation rather than dialogue-stage rebuttal; persuasiveness is not validity, source fidelity, or reply alignment.
why_relevant: Closest empirical precedent for evaluating generated arguments on both sides of an interpretive issue.

title: Can LLMs Judge Debates? Evaluating Non-Linear Reasoning via Argumentation Theory Semantics
authors: Reza Sanayei; Srdjan Vesic; Eduardo Blanco; Mihai Surdeanu
task_description: Test whether models infer argument acceptability rankings from debate-formatted texts with latent attack/support graphs.
inputs: 325 arguments and 303 relations from 12AngryMen and DebatePedia NoDE datasets; graph edges hidden.
outputs_or_labels: Rank correlation/alignment with QuAD semantics; robustness to length and discourse order.
authenticity_class: human-curated debate graphs with formal semantics
artifact_access_status: ACL paper/PDF verified; underlying NoDE artifact not separately checked
evidence_basis: ACL abstract/PDF state latent graph construction, QuAD ranking gold, 325 arguments/303 relations, and order/length robustness analysis.
limitations: Evaluates judging, not generated complete rebuttals; QuAD acceptability is not philosophical truth or authority fidelity.
why_relevant: Graph-level evaluator for support/attack consistency in generated responses.

title: Conclusion-based Counter-Argument Generation
authors: Sougata Saha; Souvick Saha; Souvik Das; Niloy Ganguly
task_description: Generate counter-arguments by explicitly modeling the source conclusion and enforcing opposite stance.
inputs: Argument text with an identifiable conclusion and stance.
outputs_or_labels: Generated counter-arguments evaluated for stance opposition and counter-argument quality.
artifact_access_status: ACL paper/PDF verified; reusable benchmark package not independently located
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states the method explicitly models the argument conclusion and enforces an opposite stance for effective counter-argument generation.
limitations: Evaluation study rather than a clearly released benchmark artifact; does not provide typed multi-turn rebuttal stages, evidence provenance, or one-to-one reply labels.
why_relevant: Directly tests a structured response constraint—countering the source conclusion rather than producing generic disagreement.
